requirements.quote: There are only two types of endpoints in QUIC: client and server.
requirements.condition: When classifying an endpoint participating in a QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the endpoint as either a client or a server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use any endpoint type other than client or server.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's endpoint type model or runtime roles can be inspected to verify that only these two classifications exist.

requirements.quote: Client: The endpoint that initiates a QUIC connection.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates a QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the initiating endpoint as the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection trace can identify which endpoint initiated the connection and verify its assigned role.

requirements.quote: Server: The endpoint that accepts a QUIC connection.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint accepts a QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the accepting endpoint as the server.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection trace can identify which endpoint accepted the connection and verify its assigned role.

requirements.quote: QUIC packet: A complete processable unit of QUIC that can be encapsulated in a UDP datagram.
requirements.condition: When an implementation treats encoded data as a QUIC packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the QUIC packet as a complete processable QUIC unit suitable for encapsulation in a UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet parsing and UDP payload construction can be tested to determine whether each recognized QUIC packet is a complete processable unit encapsulated within a UDP datagram.

requirements.quote: One or more QUIC packets can be encapsulated in a single UDP datagram.
requirements.condition: When constructing or parsing a UDP datagram carrying QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Support a UDP datagram containing one or more QUIC packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Datagrams containing one packet and multiple packets can be supplied to verify construction and parsing support.

requirements.quote: Ack-eliciting packet: A QUIC packet that contains frames other than ACK, PADDING, and CONNECTION_CLOSE.
requirements.condition: When classifying whether a QUIC packet is ack-eliciting.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify a packet as ack-eliciting when it contains at least one frame other than ACK, PADDING, or CONNECTION_CLOSE.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not classify a packet as ack-eliciting solely because it contains ACK, PADDING, or CONNECTION_CLOSE frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets with controlled frame combinations can be passed through acknowledgment classification logic and their resulting classification inspected.

requirements.quote: These cause a recipient to send an acknowledgment; see Section 13.2.1.
requirements.condition: When a recipient receives an ack-eliciting packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Cause an acknowledgment to be sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime trace can deliver an ack-eliciting packet and observe whether the recipient subsequently sends an acknowledgment.

requirements.quote: Frames are contained in QUIC packets.
requirements.condition: When encoding or representing a QUIC frame on the wire.
requirements.required_behavior: Contain the frame within a QUIC packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transmit a frame as a standalone protocol unit outside a QUIC packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Wire output and packet parsers can be inspected to verify that frames occur only as contents of QUIC packets.

requirements.quote: Address: When used without qualification, the tuple of IP version, IP address, and UDP port number that represents one end of a network path.
requirements.condition: When representing an unqualified address for one end of a network path.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the address using the tuple of IP version, IP address, and UDP port number.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's path-address representation can be inspected for the three specified tuple components.

requirements.quote: Each endpoint selects one or more connection IDs for its peer to include in packets sent towards the endpoint.
requirements.condition: For each endpoint participating in a QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Select one or more connection IDs for the peer to include in packets sent toward that endpoint.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection state and emitted packets can be inspected to verify that each endpoint selects at least one connection ID and that its peer uses selected IDs for packets directed to it.

requirements.quote: This value is opaque to the peer.
requirements.condition: When a peer receives a connection ID selected by the other endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the connection ID as an opaque value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not depend on interpreting internal structure or semantics of the peer-selected connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Code paths handling peer-selected connection IDs can be inspected or tested with arbitrary values to detect dependencies on internal structure.

requirements.quote: Stream: A unidirectional or bidirectional channel of ordered bytes within a QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the stream either unidirectional or bidirectional and preserve byte ordering within the stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not expose stream bytes out of order.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream metadata and delivery behavior can be tested to verify directionality and ordered byte delivery.

requirements.quote: A QUIC connection can carry multiple simultaneous streams.
requirements.condition: When multiple streams are active on one QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Support carrying multiple streams simultaneously on that connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can open multiple streams on one connection and verify concurrent carriage.

requirements.quote: one or more QUIC packets can be encapsulated in a UDP datagram, which is in turn encapsulated in an IP packet.
requirements.condition: When placing QUIC packets onto the network.
requirements.required_behavior: Encapsulate one or more QUIC packets in a UDP datagram and encapsulate that UDP datagram in an IP packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Captured wire traffic can be decoded to verify the QUIC-within-UDP-within-IP encapsulation hierarchy.
